newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Birch sees NZ inflation back to mid-target next yr.
newsitem.headline: Birch sees NZ inflation back to mid-target next yr.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Thursday that inflation was expected to move back into the middle of the Reserve Bank's 0-2 percent target band next year, allowing interest rates to fall further.
Birch said in a breakfast speech in Wellington that next month's Economic and Fiscal Update from the Treasury contained no surprises but included a slight downward revision in tax forecasts.
This would in turn slightly reduce forecasts for the government's operating surplus in this and subsequent years, he said.
Birch said the economy was showing "quite remarkable" strength. "At the bottom of a business cycle, we have growth well above two percent of GDP."

Birch said the December update would confirm that "export growth is now slowing, but the economy will nonetheless rebound next year, then show solid, sustained levels of growth through to the year 2000 and beyond".

He said income-based GDP, which adds up all income, principally wages and profits, earned in the economy during the year, had risen six percent in the 1995-6 year against Treasury expectations of 5.1 percent.

Statistics New Zealand had revised its estimate of nominal expenditure-based GDP over the year to 5.5 percent from 3.9 percent. Profits rose 5.8 percent in the 1995-96 year against Treasury expectations of just two percent, versus 7.1 percent in 1995-95.

"These numbers significantly change the picture we all had until now of what happened in the past year," Birch said. "There is more momentum to growth, coming out of 1995-96, than previously anticipated. The cycle will bottom from a higher base."
